title: In Secret
text: “Oof…”

You Lazy Pig… Elena spends all her time sleeping in a hammock hung inside the carriage whenever she’s not out peddling her wares. To indulge in such a lazy slumber while lulled by the noble sway of Filolial-sama… she deserves to die a thousand deaths. Even I can’t fall asleep to this gentle rocking! I, Motoyasu, am about to go mad with jealousy.

What’s more, the Lazy Pig is taking advantage of my Father’s kindness, assuming that even as a slave, her slave mark won’t activate. Well, I’ve never actually seen Keel’s slave mark activate, though. If I ever end up with the Lazy Pig’s slave mark, I’ll kill her on the spot.
As I watched this scene, feeling increasingly irritated, my Father called out to me.
“By the way, Motoyasu-kun. It seems you have a secret plan—what are you going to do?”
“Well… it’s about time, isn’t it?”

It’s been about five days since I started peddling. I’m currently traveling through the villages and towns within Melromarc. I spread out the map and plan my route. Ideally, I’d like to cover an area I can complete in a single day.
“Then I’d like you to focus on this area and make a round trip within a day.”
“That’s fine, but… what’s the plan?”
“That’s where the secret strategy comes in. First off, you can use the portal even while inside a carriage.”
“Yeah. I think I’ve heard that before. So?”
“When I was training Yuki-chan and the others, I used it inside an inn room, and on the way back, I teleported near the inn, used ‘Concealment’ to hide, and slipped back in.”

That’s definitely true. Well, I’ll need to be a bit more creative on the way back, though. Like using my spear’s special skill to phase through walls. Even if some kind of sentry were hiding and watching me, there’s no way they’d know that the hero they were supposed to be watching is actually already gone.
“That’s quite a hassle. So?”
“The fact that we’ve been holed up in the carriage a lot these past few days will serve as a good diversion, I suppose.”
“We’ve been stuck in the carriage the whole time… though we do get to rest at inns sometimes.”

We managed to defeat a few monsters that appeared on the highway during our five-day trading trip, but my level itself is rising slowly. It’s about time I started leveling up my Father—otherwise, I’m starting to get anxious.
“Well then, I’ll leave the shopkeeper and the wagon driver in charge of holding down the fort.”
“Which one should we entrust with this—Keel or Elena?”
“I can’t quite trust that Lazy Pig.”
“Oink…?”
The pig, who had been sound asleep, snapped his eyes open and is looking this way. I just can’t trust this Lazy Pig. I have a feeling he’ll betray us at the most inopportune moment.
“You’re not invited here. Get lost!”
“Oink…”
“Now, now. There’s no end to suspicion, and he’s marked with the slave brand, so it’ll be fine. Just to be safe, maybe Yuki-chan could keep an eye on him?”
“Understood. So this time, Kou will pull the carriage, the Lazy Pig will handle the trading, and we’ll have Yuki-chan keep watch.”
“I’ll make sure to honor Lord Motoyasu’s request.”
“Kou will do his best!”

I don’t know what level the Lazy Pig is, but he’s probably strong enough to put up a decent fight. The only thing we need to watch out for is bandits or the like attacking and realizing there’s no one inside the carriage. That said, as long as Yuki-chan is keeping watch, she’ll be able to handle any strange behavior—like someone trying to exploit the hole in the slave mark—without any trouble.
“Alright, let’s go. Portal Spear!”

That’s right—our goal is to draw the watchers’ attention to the wagon by pretending to be peddlers. Filolial-sama have keen senses, and I myself can spot hidden opponents to a certain extent. It’s certain that there are no watchers inside the wagon right now. At most, they’re probably just keeping watch from outside the carriage. Since we’re moving quickly in a moving carriage, it’ll be difficult for them to pinpoint our exact location. Under these circumstances, I figured that even if someone who was supposed to be inside the carriage disappeared, no one would notice.
“Whoa! That’s amazing…”
“Boo.”
We’ve arrived in Siltvelt. This is my father’s first time using a portal.
“What should we do? Should we head straight to Siltvelt Castle?”
“Hmm… Sorry, but I’d like to level up first. I get anxious if my level isn’t high enough.”
“I suppose so. Well then, how about you go with Sakura-chan?”
Sakura-chan’s outfit is already ready, and as if she’s fully prepared, she transforms into her Filolial form.
“So, shall we go?”
“Yeah. Let’s go too, Keel.”
“Boo!”
Looking cheerful, my father climbs onto Sakura-chan’s back along with Keel.
“Well then, have a good trip. In the meantime, I’ll go retrieve the item I was supposed to give to my father.”
“Okay! Now we can level up freely.”
“Let’s go!”

With a “dap-dap-dap,” Sakura-chan ran off with my father and the others on her back. Meanwhile, I headed out to retrieve the materials I’d hidden when I’d been leveling up Yuki-chan and the others. Maybe I can pick up some decent drops along the way? No, I should just put herbs and the like into my weapon to use for alchemy.
“Wow, I was surprised at how quickly our levels shot up—it was almost funny.”
That evening, my father returned, riding on Sakura-chan’s back with a cheerful expression. I packed some of the materials I’d collected into a bag and met up with my Father.
“How’s it going?”
“Right now, I’m Lv. 18, Keel-kun is Lv. 19, and Sakura-chan is Lv. 35.”
Hmm… It’s probably because Sakura-chan’s own level is on the low side, but her progress is a bit slow.
“Tomorrow, I’ll level up Sakura-chan. It’d be better to raise her level a bit more.”
“Is that so?”
“I thought she’d go up more.”

This is a priority for now. I’m a bit worried about Yuki-chan and the Filolial-sama’s levels and stats—I’ve been too conscious of being watched. But hey, with my skills, it’ll be easy enough to raise their levels even more dramatically.
“I don’t want to get too far away from Naofumi. I can’t protect him.”
Sakura-chan is refusing. Her dedication to putting her mission first brings tears to my eyes. How endearing she is.
“Oh, I’m at a loss for words—such a noble sense of self-worth!”
“Even so…”
“Just have Yuki and Kou come along.”
“Logically, that makes sense, but… in the end, I guess we’ll just have to rely on Motoyasu-kun to level up Yuki-chan and the others…”
There are quite a few issues to deal with here. Sakura-chan’s strong sense of duty certainly plays a part, too.
“Well then, I’ll be at the carriage tomorrow. If I don’t show my face for days on end, people will get suspicious, and I think there won’t be any problems as long as I keep an eye on Elena-san.”
“Boo.”
Keel is nodding in agreement with Father’s suggestion.
“Sakura will pull the carriage!”
“That’s right. It’ll be easier for her to study alchemy and do her homework if Sakura-chan pulls it.”
“Yeah.”
“So, that’s settled. Now then, Father. Please accept the materials I’ve gathered.”
“Oh, yeah. Thanks… There’s quite a variety in here.”
“It’s still nowhere near enough to strengthen your shield, Father.”
“I thought I’d gone around quite a bit with Sakura-chan and the others today, but I’ve still got a long way to go…”
Father scratches the back of his head with a wry smile. After all, the goal this time is to secretly make my Father stronger as soon as possible.

“It goes without saying, but the medicinal herbs growing wild around here are different from those in Melromarc. The monsters are different, and the drops are different, too. It’s a relief that some of them are treated the same in the potion recipes, but actually making them will probably be a different story.”
“I suppose we’ll just have to learn as we go.”

That said, I don’t really know much about alchemy myself, since I just have Yari make the potions for me. Well, even if there are a few oddities, I don’t think we’ll be identified as peddlers. After all, only a Hero can verify that the items are actually crafted from weapons. As I was thinking about this, my Father placed the materials I’d given him into the shield.
“There are plenty of ways to enhance it, but is this current shield really good enough? It seems like there’d be less waste if we waited until a slightly better shield turned up…”
“Isn’t choosing the best option each time and making it stronger what being a gamer is all about?”
That’s exactly the kind of thing my future Father would say.
“Well, you’re right. I tend to forget this, but if I just wait for a better shield to come along, I’ll never get any stronger.”
My Father nodded repeatedly as he seemed to decide which shield to enhance.
“I’ll just strengthen it enough to get by for now… okay.”
“If there are any materials needed for the upgrade, just give Motoyasu the order whenever you need them, and I’ll go get them.”
“Thanks. Well, this might end up being a waste of time, but I’ll leave the necessary materials up to you.”

My future father told me which ores were needed for the shield he’s currently upgrading. If I gather those, his strength will become rock-solid. Well, either way, my Father will need to level up himself, though.
“Hmm, it’s about time.”
“Yeah. Motoyasu-kun. Please.”
“Understood. Portal Spear!”

Using my teleportation skill, we flew to the spot where we were supposed to meet up with Yuki-chan and the others. Of course, I could see a glimpse of the situation at the location I chose just before teleporting. Just as planned, the carriage was waiting for our return. Now it’s just a matter of timing the jump. If we activate our stealth skill beforehand, we can cover our tracks to some extent.

However… Father’s orders are quite a hassle. I think we could avoid all this trouble if we just killed everyone keeping watch, but there’s nothing we can do about it. After teleporting through the portal, we got into the carriage and then deactivated our stealth skill.
